chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to bury his hair in his tent in Mina and say, 'They used to prefer that.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) disliked that the hair be taken out of Mecca, saying, 'Whoever takes it out, he must return it.'

key_terms.فُسْطَاط: Tent or dwelling, specifically referring to the tents used by pilgrims in Mina.
key_terms.مِنًى: A sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj.
key_terms.يَرُدَّهُ: He must return it (to its place of origin, i.e., Mecca/Mina).
key_terms.يَسْتَحِبُّونَ: They preferred or considered it recommended (mustahabb).
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: He disliked (karahah), indicating a recommended dislike rather than prohibition.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on disposing of hair cut during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic preference (istihbab) for burying ritual hair in Mina, a practice attributed to Ali ibn al-Husayn and the early Muslims to maintain the sanctity of the holy precincts. Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling that hair removed from Mecca must be returned underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving the ritual purity and symbolic integrity of the Hajj sites, distinguishing between mere removal and proper disposal.
